sections.overview: Phalangium opilio, the Common Harvestman, is an arachnid in the order Opiliones; harvestmen are not spiders.
sections.identification: It has long legs and a variable pale body pattern; males have a distinctive horn-like projection on the chelicerae.
sections.habitat: It lives in open vegetated sites, including field margins, meadows and gardens.
sections.diet: It preys on small arthropods, including aphids and insect eggs.
sections.behavior: It is mainly active at dusk and night.
sections.reproduction: Fertilization is internal; females lay eggs in soil, and no further parental care is reported.
sections.ecology: In crops it can prey on pests; laboratory results show diet affects its development and reproduction.
sections.conservation: The sources consulted describe it as widespread or abundant in several regions; no global conservation assessment was found for this draft.
